messages:
eng-oncall-bot: PAGER — severity: P2. us-west1 GPU capacity critical. Autoscaler failing to provision new GPU instances -> queue depth spiked to 3.1k, tail latency >10s, ~80% generation requests throttled. Paging on-call.

Marta G.: I’m on it. jumping in. initial triage: autoscaler logs show quota error: "quotaExceeded for GPUs in region us-west1".

Liam R.: confirmed from metrics — token throughput collapsed ~ 17:02 UTC, queues started growing around 17:00 UTC. All Dedicated pools in us-west1 at 100% and pending scale-up stuck.

Sofia P.: @Ava (infra) can you check cloud console for quota/limit events? I suspect GCP GPU quota got exhausted or a soft limit prevented new instances.

Ava (infra): on it. Opening GCP console now. Also filing support case.

Ava (infra): quick note — GCP reports regional GPU quota hit for us-west1 (NVIDIA A100). There’s also an internal project limit at 24 GPUs remaining that we accidentally set low during the last month’s cleanup.

Marta G.: Ok, mitigation plan in order: 1) immediate traffic shaping / throttling to reduce queue growth, 2) shift non-critical workloads to other regions (us-east1), 3) enable fallback models (smaller quantized) for best-effort customers, 4) request quota increase with GCP and open urgent support.

Liam R.: Implementing step 1: temporary rate-limit rule across hosted API for non-enterprise keys. Setting per-key token cap to 30 tokens/sec. Patch below:
```json
POST /admin/ratelimits
{
  "scope":"hosted-api",
  "filter":"tier!=enterprise",
  "token_rate":30
}
```

Sofia P.: Step 2: shifting some traffic to us-east1. Will adjust smart-routing policy to divert 25% of new sessions. Running route change now.

Sofia P.: route weights updated: us-west1=0.75, us-east1=0.25. Observing drop in queue growth, but us-east1 CPU is rising — fine for now.

Marta G.: Step 3: enable fallback model for chat generation for low-tier customers — flip feature flag redwood.fallback.small-model = on. This reduces GPU memory and allows more instances to handle requests.

Liam R.: Command to flip flag:
```bash
redwood feature toggle set redwood.fallback.small-model true --scope=hosted
```
Flag flip done. Fallback now active — dropped GPU memory per-session ~40%.

Ava (infra): GCP support case created (case 123456789). Requested quota increase and removal of manual project limit. They replied ETA 1-2 hours for approval; escalated to phone support.

PagerDuty: Incident timeline created: INC-2026-03014-01. Please add timeline updates to the incident doc.

Marta G.: Customer impact note: in the last 15 minutes we observed increased 429s for hosted API keys (non-enterprise). A handful of sessions for enterprise customers experienced degraded latency but no full errors due to reserved capacity. Need comms to affected customers in the next 30 minutes.

Sofia P.: Real-time impact numbers: 17:05 UTC window: 2,900 requests dropped, 1,200 requests degraded (slower). Top affected region: us-west1. Top affected product: chat-completions.

Liam R.: Manual scale-up attempt blocked by the quota. I tried to spin up a smaller VM type with A10s as a stopgap but cluster autoscaler refuses due to node selector constraints in deployment config. We can patch to allow A10-backed nodes temporarily.

Marta G.: Go ahead, Liam. Patch the nodeSelector to allow a10 GPU families for non-enterprise pools only. Also ensure we keep the KV cache warm.

Liam R.: Patch applied to k8s autoscaling group. For reference:
```yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        accelerator: "a10"
      tolerations: ...
```
New nodes requested; waiting for nodes to register.

Ava (infra): GCP updated — quota increased by 40 A100 GPUs in us-west1 (provisioning), and the manual project cap was removed. ETA for new A100s hitting our quota: ~18 minutes. Phone support still on the line.

Marta G.: Good. Next: keep routing adjustments and throttles in place until new capacity online. We will remove fallback flag only after stable queues for 10 minutes.

Sofia P.: Status update 17:21 UTC: queue length down from 3.1k -> 900 since throttle + route shift + fallback. Latency improving but still above SLOs.

Liam R.: The temporary A10 nodes came up but they have lower perf; they reduced queue by ~200. Useful short-term.

Ava (infra): GCP says the A100s are provisioning; they appear in console and are being allocated to our project. Autoscaler now sees remaining quota. Starting scale actions to create GPU-backed nodes.

Marta G.: once new nodes join, we will: 1) gradually move traffic back to us-west1 with 5% increments, 2) remove token throttle for enterprise keys, 3) monitor error budget. Do not remove fallback until stable.

Sofia P.: 17:35 UTC: new A100 nodes registered, scheduler draining A10 temporary nodes, pods rescheduled onto A100 nodes. Queue now 120 and dropping.

Marta G.: rolling rollback of routing: us-west1 -> us-east1 weight moved back to 0.9 us-west1, 0.1 us-east1. Removing non-enterprise throttle in 5 min window — hold.

Liam R.: Removing non-enterprise throttle now as capacity stable for 5+ minutes.

Sofia P.: Monitoring: 17:40 UTC last 5m error rate back to normal for most customers. Enterprise unaffected throughout.

Marta G.: Incident status -> mitigated. Root cause: regional GPU quota exhaustion + an unintended low internal project GPU cap meant autoscaler couldn't acquire GPUs; secondary cause: autoscaler nodeSelector constraints prevented immediate fallback to alternative GPU family.

Marta G.: Action items (assigned):
- Ava: follow up with GCP to confirm permanency of quota increase and request quota elasticity in peak windows.
- Liam: update k8s autoscaler config to allow mixed GPU families for emergency fallback and add automated A10 fallback policy.
- Sofia: prepare customer comms for affected hosted users and internal postmortem summary.
- Engineering: add alert for internal project caps and a runbook step to verify cloud quota before autoscale.

Ava (infra): I’ll also request quotas in multiple regions proactively and add a CI job to detect manual caps during infra changes.

PagerDuty: Incident moved to resolved->monitoring. Please link to incident doc INC-2026-03014-01 in postmortem.

Marta G.: Thanks everyone. Closing on-call handoff note: @Liam you own the infra followup, @Ava work with GCP, @Sofia write the comms. I’ll kick off postmortem template. :white_check_mark:

Sofia P.: Adding quick timeline to ticket and starting draft for customers (apology + root cause + remediation + ETA for permanent fix).

eng-oncall-bot: Incident closed for on-call at 17:50 UTC.
